newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan dollar closes lower, but downtrend limited.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan dollar closes lower, but downtrend limited.

text.p: The Taiwan dollar continued its recent downturn on Tuesday, finishing lower to reflect of a firming U.S. dollar overseas, but dealers said local currency's near-term downside was limited.
The local unit closed at T$27.880 against Monday's T$27.862 finish. Turnover through dealers was US$197 million.

The U.S. dollar's strong showing against the yen and the mark overseas triggered demand for the American currency, but suspected central bank intervention smoothed the local unit's fall, dealers said.

"It's apparent the central bank is trying to smooth the Taiwan dollar depreciation," said one dealer at a foreign bank. "The market would like to test T$27.9, but everyone knows the central bank is quite capable of defending the Taiwan dollar."

Dealers said the Taiwan dollar remained in a slowly depreciating trend, but would not immediately test eight-year support at T$28 due to strong expectations that the central bank would orchestrate an intervention if it did.
A range of T$27.85-90 was seen for Wednesday.
